name: Paper, tissue and paperboard products
note: For basic sanitary, tissue, and wrapping papers, CBP consistently holds that the production of the bulk parent rolls confers origin, while subsequent unwinding, embossing, printing, cutting to size, folding, and re-rolling are minor converting operations that do not substantially transform the paper. Conversely, for structured or shaped articles like file folders, gift bags, rigid boxes, labels, and molded tableware, die-cutting, molding, pleating, and forming the paper into a distinct new article confer origin. Written from 45 CBP substantial-transformation rulings outside every development and held-out split (D660); every cited ruling was checked against its facts and holding. Costs are illustrative defaults; users edit them.

groups.name: Parent rolls
operations: Process wood pulp into single or multi-ply paper, tissue, or paperboard sheet
Finish and wind base paper into bulk parent or jumbo rolls

precedent.note: CBP held that manufacturing the parent roll confers origin when downstream work is limited to tissue or wrap converting (N339156, N341898, N344612), but not when the roll is later die-cut, pleated, or molded into a distinct article (N335200, N347648, N348208).

groups.name: Printing and decoration
operations: Print colors, patterns, or logos onto paper stock or overlay sheets
Apply foil stamping, glitter decoration, or protective lamination to paper

precedent.note: Printing, foil stamping, and laminating paper stock did not confer origin on wrapping paper or tissue (N339156, N347987, N347988), nor did pre-printing paper sheets that were sent to another country to be formed into bags or boxes (N333537, N334032).

groups.name: Fasteners and accessories
operations: Produce metal folder fasteners, hanging rods, and hooks
Produce plastic clips, clear plastic tabs, handles, decorative pompoms, and cardboard cores

precedent.note: Supplying decorative pompoms, hanging rods, or handles from another country did not confer origin on the finished paper products (N345915, N347187, N347189).

groups.name: Die-cutting and moulding
operations: Die-cut paper or paperboard into folder, box, label, or circular blanks
Mold paper blanks into three-dimensional plates or pleated cups with rolled rims
Continuous-pleat and heat-press paper rolls into accordion window shade bodies
Apply die-cut adhesive labels to printed release liner sheets or microperforate cardstock

precedent.note: CBP held that die-cutting, molding, or pleating flat paper or paperboard into structured shapes such as gift bags, boxes, shades, labels, folders, or cups substantially transforms the paper (N333537, N334032, N335200, N345972, N347648, N348208).

groups.name: Converting, folding and packing
operations: Unwind, emboss, perforate, slit to width, cut to length, and fold or rewind tissue and paper rolls onto cores
Fold and glue cut paperboard blanks into finished bags, boxes, or folders
Attach handles, metal fasteners, hanging rods, adhesive strips, or decorative trim
Perform quality control and package into retail units

precedent.note: Simple converting of parent rolls by embossing, cutting to length and width, folding, and rewinding was not enough to confer origin (N341898, N344612, N344620, N344621, N345915, N347059), whereas folding, gluing, and assembling die-cut blanks into bags, boxes, and folders in the same plant as the cutting conferred origin (N333537, N334032, N347645, N347648).
